title: [CQ-RF06b] VS Code protected daemon spawn
description:
Objective: under the protected profile, the VS Code extension starts the Moe daemon only from the runtime installed with the extension. This mirrors JetBrains MoeDaemonSupervisor.protectedDaemonCommand / protectedDaemonEnvironment / protectedCommandOrRefuse. Split out of CQ-RF06 (task-98ffe33f448746e6bc802db0b5624fd0) by architect-bd1eb82d on 2026-10-30 to keep each diff under the 400-LOC review cap. RF06 lands the shared policy as exported functions in moe-vscode/src/services/MoeDaemonClient.ts: runtimeProfile (strict, fail-closed, session pin), comparablePath/isWithin, installedRoot(extensionPath) = <extensionPath>/bundled and installedArtifact. This row consumes them in the same file.

Deliverable: when runtimeProfile(projectPath) is 'protected', MoeDaemonClient.startDaemon:
1. Selects the daemon with installedArtifact(installedRoot, 'daemon/index.js', projectPath). resolveGlobalConfigDaemonPath and any project copy are never consulted.
2. Selects node as an absolute, real, regular file outside the project (a mirror of JetBrains installedExecutable). It tries, in this order:
   - MOE_NODE_COMMAND;
   - on non-Windows, ~/.local/share/moe/node/current/bin/node;
   - an in-process lookup of node or node.exe over PATH entries that are absolute and outside the project (never a bare name resolved by spawn);
   - on Windows, the resolveNodeExecutable candidates (ProgramFiles, ProgramFiles(x86), LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\nodejs, LOCALAPPDATA\nvm\current, APPDATA\nvm).
3. Spawns [node, daemon, 'start', '--project', projectPath] with cwd = the installed daemon's directory. The env drops NODE_OPTIONS and NODE_PATH, and PATH (matched case-insensitively on Windows) keeps only absolute entries outside the project.
4. Refuses instead of falling back: any rejection starts nothing, logs the reason and shows `Protected execution profile: <reason>. Project and PATH copies of the Moe daemon are not used.`
5. The legacy profile is byte-for-byte unchanged.

Out of scope:
- Running-daemon provenance (JetBrains activationRefusal, spawn records, RF03 replacement). VS Code under protected still connects to an existing daemon.json daemon. Node has no portable process start-time API, so this stays a known gap, recorded for CQ-RF07.
- Persistent state, JetBrains changes, .moe edits, enabling verified-local.

Constraint: five test harnesses (daemon-start, daemon-json-cap, approval-paths, plan-approval-client, settings-wire) transpile MoeDaemonClient.ts alone with a closed require shim. Add no new local runtime import to MoeDaemonClient.ts.

Verification command (fresh, exit 0 required): cd moe-vscode && npm test && npm run compile
definitionOfDone: Under the protected profile, startDaemon spawns exactly [real node outside the project, real installed bundled/daemon/index.js, 'start', '--project', projectPath], with cwd = the installed daemon dir and an env without NODE_OPTIONS, NODE_PATH or relative/project PATH entries. Shown by tests in a new moe-vscode/tests/*.test.cjs.

Under the protected profile, a missing installed daemon, or no acceptable node, spawns nothing, shows the 'Protected execution profile: … Project and PATH copies of the Moe daemon are not used.' refusal, and never consults the global-config daemon. Shown by tests.
The legacy profile behaves exactly as before: the existing daemon-start tests pass unchanged.
The verification command exits 0 with its output supplied to complete_task.

Fresh output of this exact command is the complete_task verification evidence.

Adversarial self-review of this task's diff only (load the adversarial-self-review skill). Check that:

(a) Under protected, no code path spawns a bare 'node' or a project or global-config daemon. Grep the protected branch for resolveDaemonRuntime and resolveGlobalConfigDaemonPath.
(b) The first found node candidate is validated, and a rejection refuses with no silent fallback.
(c) The env is a COPY: process.env is never mutated.
(d) Windows PATH and NODE_* keys are handled case-insensitively, with exactly one PATH spelling left.
(e) cwd is the installed daemon dir, never the workspace.
(f) The legacy spawn options and messages are byte-identical, as D7 and the existing harnesses show.
(g) No absolute path in a UI message; paths go to log() only.
(h) No new local import in MoeDaemonClient.ts.

Report in the completion summary:
- the net LOC (target about 250, under 400);
- the VS Code running-daemon provenance gap (no activationRefusal parity), recorded on RF07 task-f3f364a6.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: This row was split from RF06 to stay under the 400-LOC review cap. The policy lives in MoeDaemonClient.ts (RF06's decision), because five vm harnesses transpile that file alone with a closed require shim. A separate module or extension.ts injection was rejected: the import breaks the harnesses, and an unwired client would fail open. --host 0.0.0.0 is omitted because VS Code has no WSL agent toggle. Running-daemon provenance is out of scope (no portable process start-time API in Node) and is recorded on RF07.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: Legacy startDaemon picks bundled, then the global-config daemon, and node from resolveDaemonRuntime (MOE_NODE_COMMAND, else the managed node on non-Windows, else a bare 'node'). It spawns detached with stdio ignore. ensureDaemonRunning passes 'init' when .moe is missing. Under protected, .moe/project.json exists or a session pin holds, and JetBrains always uses 'start'. JetBrains daemonPath prepends node's dir and appends the bootstrap dirs, then protectedDaemonEnvironment filters PATH to absolute non-project entries.
planningNotes.risks:
- Windows env-key casing: a spread copy of process.env is case-sensitive. JetBrains hit a duplicate PATH/Path spelling that broke git, so keep exactly one spelling.
- The macOS tmpdir realpath differs from its path, so tests must compare realpaths.
- The non-Windows fixed candidates (/usr/bin/node and others) exist on CI hosts. Tests that need a 'nothing found' answer must use windows=true units (D5), not the real filesystem.
- RF06 must have landed: this task depends on it, and both edit the same file.

completionSummary:
Protected VS Code daemon startup now accepts only real installed bundled/daemon/index.js and an absolute real regular Node file outside the project. Node discovery follows override, executable managed Node, protected in-process PATH, then OS/nvm fallbacks; the first found candidate is validated with no silent fallback after refusal. Spawns 'start' with installed daemon cwd and copied env removing NODE_OPTIONS/NODE_PATH, unsafe PATH entries and duplicate Windows PATH spellings. Refusals spawn nothing and never consult legacy/global-config resolvers.
Legacy startDaemon bytes are unchanged except protected dispatch; imports and existing tests unchanged. 17 new tests cover D1–D7, async errors, concurrency, discovery order, symlink refusal and error containment. Review fixed PATH realpath-error swallowing and nvm directory-link discovery with failing regressions first. Scratch baseline 17/17; 11/11 mutants assertion-killed.
Final Linux tests 284/284, zero failures/skips. Final native Windows exact gate exit 0: 284 tests, 280 pass, 0 fail, 4 platform skips; tsc exit 0. Toolchain deviation: attempted planned Linux gate; compile cannot load the absent @typescript/typescript-linux-x64. Used installed native Windows TS7 via cmd.exe, as RF06 did, without modifying dependencies. Logs /tmp/rf06b-final-{linux,windows}.log.
Net +373 LOC (+376/-3): MoeDaemonClient.ts +137/-3; new protected-daemon-spawn.test.cjs 239 lines. All files attributed in complete_step; wrapper owns landing. No Git writes, direct repository .moe edits, peer changes or verified-local enablement.
Known VS Code running-daemon provenance gap (no activationRefusal parity) remains recorded on RF07 task-f3f364a6. Handoff and gotcha memories saved.

Require fully qualified, drive-independent Windows entries before retaining PATH. Audit installedExecutable's identical check at line 227; keep legacy behavior unchanged.

Add cases for single-leading backslash and slash entries with host/daemon cwd on different drives; require rejection and retain safe drive-qualified/UNC paths. The native-Windows scratch repro in the rejection reason currently fails. Re-run Linux tests and the recorded Windows test+compile gate.
